guidetextdraw._value:
TAX IMPLICATIONS OF FEE WAIVER

IRC Section 117(d) Qualified Tuition Reduction applies to any reduction in tuition provided by California State University (CSU) to either an employee for the education of an employee or the dependent child or spouse of the employee. A qualified  tuition reduction is tax-free only if it is for education below the graduate level, except for graduate students engaged in  teaching or research at the CSU.

If the educational institution requires the recipient of the qualified tuition reduction to provide teaching and or research services to that institution in return for the tuition reduction, the benefit becomes taxable.

IRC Section 127/Educational Assistance Program applies to educational assistance benefits to employees only, up to a maximum of $5,250 per calendar year. Exclusion applies to graduate level courses.

Note that the course level determines taxability, not the education level of the employee.
guidetextdraw.name: textdraw1614667691004

guidetextdraw_985905113._value:
*All graduate-level employees receiving a benefit of over $5,250 in a calendar year will be treated as taxable and will be subject to withholding taken from the employee’s pay warrant. The employees may consult a personal tax advisor to determine if courses taken are deductible on their tax return.

The waived fee amount determined to be taxable should be included as wages on the employee’s Form W-2 and applicable taxes withheld. The imputed taxable income is typically reported by the 10th of the month following the date of the constructive receipt to the State Controller’s Office (SCO), which is the semester’s census date. The usage of the campus census date as the “constructive receipt” of the fee waiver benefit is to eliminate adverse tax reporting on imputed income when an employee’s dependent drops courses.

Currently, the flat tax rate is 36.25% comprised of: federal tax (22%), state tax (6.6%), Social Security tax (6.2%), and Medicare tax (1.45%); and may be adjusted annually.

You will be notified via email in advance before the taxes are withheld from your pay warrant.

Please refer to the Fee Waiver & Reduction Program/Administrative Guide issued by the Office of the Chancellor for additional information.
guidetextdraw_985905113.name: textdraw_9859051131614667794112

I certify that the individual noted above is my legal dependent, child/spouse or registered domestic partner. I wish to transfer my fee waiver eligibility, as provided in appropriate policy or collective bargaining agreement, to my dependent child/spouse or domestic partner listed above.

I understand this transfer prohibits my personal use of fee waiver benefits during the period indicted. 

Under current IRS regulations, the dependent fee waiver benefit is not taxable for undergraduate dependent children or spouse coursework. The benefit is taxable for graduate dependent children, spouse, and undergraduate and graduate domestic partner coursework. This taxation is applied to the employee who transfers the benefit and is reported as taxable income on their check warrant.
